notes.title: The final release build is now being uploaded!
notes.notes:
Since we released the bigger world we have pushed out small chunks of updates to fill in the gaps and now we are uploading our final release build. There are some minor bugs that are being fixed as we speak, but they shouldn't affect the game play as a whole.

We hope that this new build is available for everyone by tomorrow (it takes some time for steam to process).

This release build features:

*4 characters
*A caribbean world with islands/caves/other areas
*Enemy ships
*Build (ships etc)
*Mine (mine gold, iron)
*Quests
*Levels
*Caves
*Cannibals

Our goal was to create a game featuring building/mining/exploring and that is what this game is all about. 

I also wanted to update the first game and this new sequel is a both a new update and a new game.

However, we have decided to include a bigger story and include more items / armor and a lot of other things. But that will be included in a bigger update in a few months.


I would also like to include what I wanted to create from the start. A survival mode. 

In the end this game will feature these titles/gamemodes:

HoD franchise:

On open seas (our core game that we will focus on)
A pirate adventure ( a new pirate survival gamemode)
A ship adventure ( a new update from the old game)

notes.title: Tomorrow we are opening up the big world.
notes.notes:
For a while now we have had a small version out on the store page of On open seas and now we are opening up the big world.

After this we will prepare the game for the big release 24th of December.

notes.title: Alright, let's clear this all up. You know me...
notes.notes:
I usually do not respond directly to these things but now I felt like I had to.

Sometimes I visit the store page and look for new things that people have said or if people have suggestions in general.

Now I see that some are a bit skeptical towards this whole thing that we're trying to do.

I usually say that people who are skeptical are normally very self-centered and do not really care about others. Hopefully I am wrong. 

But let's face all of these questions that some people seem to have, I have been honest all the way (personally) and I will continue to be so.

Ok, let's begin.

First, the price, 

Yes, it could be lower. But if you need to pay people for doing things, it just doesn't add up having a low price. - And frankly when we release the game it will be roughly 4-5 GB in content, in which - We have created ourselves. Other teams with lower quality products takes much more for their games.

But I am going to lower my guard on this one. The price will be changed to 8 € and stay there, from now on. (Not when there are steam sales though)

Right now the original game is available and a test version of the new game.

So right now you are actually receiving 1,5 games. (roughly). The original game is included and it is never going to be removed.

The first game was a disaster yes, but that is why I am personally working to make it right - Haha, I still hope I am wrong with the "only care about themselves thing". 

Things take time, and if you don't get it right the first time, then you always have the right to make it right the second time. 

The first game is being remade from scratch and I believe it will be a great product once it is done.

I do not really understand why the current game would be a disaster when it is not even out? We have given you a taste of the new sequel/update and prepared the store for it.

Not many would give out 3 games in one - I do this because I believe in you guys and because you shouldn't need to pay for three games that is a part of the same theme and story.

 haha, the December deadline will hold. Don't you worry about that! The game is very much finished. But I don''t want  to make any mistakes, everything has to be perfect.

why are w carrying on "updating" the first game instead of learning from it and moving on to pastures new?

Because, this is very simple and you should all know this!

You should NEVER have a bad product out on the market - You continue improving it until over 90 % of the customers are happy and positive about the product. You should never abandon something, you finish it and you make it great. No matter how long time that goes. 

I never give up, and nor should you. I started this project 2 years ago, believing I wouldn't have to spend that much time on it. Now I've spent roughly 60 % of my time for two years on this to make this launch as great as possible. I won't back down, never will.

This below I need to clear up:

"why change a game name, blaming it on people calling it "hands on d*ck" when literally no evidence of the such exists on the store page while still having HoD in the title and having Hands on Deck ALLLLLLLLLLL over the store page?"

This is also very simple, I have deleted all of the discussions and comments about this - Just because of the fact that it went crazy and it's not good to have such language on a store page...  HoD is always a part of the games, the new game is a sequel of the original game.. Like it's literally the same except you play as a character instead of as a ship.

So yeah, simple - I took it all away so that you wouldn't need to see it. But hey, if you don't believe me... (Which by the way you should, since I am trying my very best and you all know this to be true)

Here: 
[img]https://i.gyazo.com/83e614fa8af9d4343441fab534f43290.png[/img]

Let me try at least to make this awesome again. And yes, the old game was a failure and if you think in terms of what is wrong/right etc the absolutely best thing to do is to rename everything and start from scratch. To make this game into what it is supposed to be. But we didn't do that. We're sticking to the original name and making it more "sequel based".

The original game is available and the easiest way to get it is just to right klick on the game go to properties and then choose "HandsOnDeck". 

yes, it's just that simple.

We will deliver 24th of December. There is no point of bashing before that date.

This is like literally, my child. and I will do the best I can to make you all satisfied.


I feel very confident that those of you who are skeptical about this will change your mind after 24th of December.

This is how it is going to be, and it is the right thing to do.

Also, it is great that you speak out. I just watched a video a person linked in a review that was from 2015. That guy spoke about the steering system being slippery etc - I actually had no idea that people didn't like that and I had no thoughts of improving it at all.

In the end, you are all making this product the way it should be. I will probably give you something in return for that. That's at least something I should..

Squadleader32 out,

notes.title: Today we are announcing HoD: On open seas!
notes.notes:
We have prepared the store for On open seas and the first version is now available to download!

Clearly based on the reviews from the old game, we had to act and create something greater, much greater. That is what we are doing right now.

Today we are announcing major changes to our product "Hands on Deck". 
Be prepared to be amazed.


[img]https://i.gyazo.com/bf1a9583d15dcf2aa988b3f7535d5088.jpg[/img]


First of all,

We are going to release a huge update for the old game 24th of December, it is going to be much greater than we ever would have thought it could be.

But we also have some other stuff going on as well.

During this time (Since the launch of the first game in July 2015) we have created 2 other games that we are going to include here.

We are really excited about this!

Our main title that we are really proud of is going to be called HoD: On open seas and is going to be sort of a sequel.

It is based on the same mechanics as the old game. But we didn't stop there, it is a whole new game including things you never have seen before.

We have also started to send out the first versions of this to everyone who has purchased the old game.

We really believe that HoD: On open seas can really change the way people see our products on Steam. That is why we will let this game take over the whole store page.

The old game will always be available and we are really excited about the update towards that game as well. You can see more about it in the store description.

And one more thing.

We have also created a whole new game that is really breaking out of the things that we have done in the past. This game has been made from scratch in Unreal Engine and we are planning to release it as soon as possible.

The name: A pirate adventure 

So as of today, you will be able to test out the new game for a short while before we release the first parts of the new update 2.0 and HoD: On open seas.

*Everything we release will be available for free of charge. However HoD: On open seas will have a lot of things going on and we do not have the resources to release everything as one. Therefore we have to release expansion packs for that game in the future. But we will give out those things for free to customers who has shown loyalty and who has bought the game before 30th of November.

notes.title: About the old game.
notes.notes:
I (Squadleader32) did not quite think through the old version of the game.

I did a huge mistake by launching it on Steam so early - Clearly based on all the reviews. The old game wasn't finished on time.

However, one year later I stand as strong as ever and I have decided to recreate the old game all by myself once the version 2.0 is out.

I have a lot of ideas I want to implement into the original game - And I will do it.

My goal is to have high quality applications on PC, Mac and Linux.

The only way to achieve that is to continue to update all of my products on Steam until it reaches near the ultimate perfection. 

One year ago I did not know much about game developing and I was "learning as I go".

Now we have a full team that has experience and knowledge in:

Unity
Unreal Engine
UDK
Xamarin
Visual Studio
3ds Max
Blender
Maya
MotionBuilder
Music editing of all kinds
Sound editing

Programming skills:

C#
C++
Java
HTML5
Python

We have also purchased additional tools to help us in the developement, such as:

*High quality 3d-printers
*VR technology
*Animating tools (converting real world motion to animations)

That is why we strongly believe that we can achieve the goals we have set for this product.

We will not stop until those goals are filled.


I really want to thank all those people that supports us, both in our lives and in this community.

Squadleader32 out,

PS. (sorry for the "update-bombs")

notes.title: New engine
notes.notes:
Since we have started to get the "test version" out to people now we have been able to get a lot of feedback!

What we have noticed is that the game is very heavy and it requires at least a NVIDIA GTX 660 in order to run the game smoothly.

However, we have been in the works of converting the game from Unity into another engine that is somewhat of a "mixup" between our own and Unreal Engine.

The results:

Unity3D

[img]https://i.gyazo.com/ccce701eea0c546d43ce646217e1aa5d.jpg[/img]

A Mix-up between Unreal Engine 4 and our own
[img]https://i.gyazo.com/aae0711d980c0061de46eed40575669a.png[/img]


Our goal was to be able to run the game smoothly (somwhat at least) on a LAPTOP with INTEL GRAPHIS HD 4000 card and a intel i5 330 processor. 

The results are...

7 FPS with Unity when playing on the first island
40 FPS with Unreal/Mixed when playing on the first island

Both scenes were identical in every way possible.

The laptop we used:

ASUS ZENBOOK UX32A

notes.title: Reviews and insight
notes.notes:
Some people have been really disappointed with the game, the outcome of their reviews is "boring and same thing all over again". So far there has been only two official "real" reviews, that I am aware of.

Of course I have been talking to many people that owns this game and I always support critisism, and everything anyone says - We will take into consideration and the outcome will probably be "We will do what you say".

To clearify,

My name is Henrik (Squadleader32), 6 months ago I didn't know programming at all, I didn't know Unity at all or web-development at all. But I really wanted to create this game. I learned everything i could during the creation of this game. I have created 99 % of the game and written all the scripts myself, created all the models and the gameplay, I didn't even know how to create game models.

But I have been given the oppertunity to get help from other people, such as the old developers from Overboard, developers from Unity themselves and others.

However, I am still learning and so does the company HJO Creations. This is our first game - that we use as a learning stage in this process.

I can admit one thing, a couple of people pointed out that this game should have been in the "early development" section. That would probably have been a better way of doing this.

Unfortunately you can not revert this decision, but now I have learned that, and will not to that again in our upcoming titles.

I have a lot planned for this game, Update 2.0 will contain a lot of changes that will make this game into what it is supposed to be.

This version that is out now is "the base idea". That is the idea I built in my mind the first time I thought of creating this game. But during the development process I have thought up of a lot of other things that is going to change this game completely.

To summarize, I am 20 years of age, I have been working for almost 14 hours a day for 6 months on this game, I am currently running 2 companies and it's probably not that great to do so, but well, it happened.

This game will change A LOT the coming weeks and we hope to get from 400 mb of content to 6 gb of content within the timeframe 6-10 weeks.

I am not developing alone anymore, I have some people helping me including friends and my fellow co-founders in HJO Creations. 

But I really appreciate that you point out the things you don't like, but please take a look at the creators first, what are their capabilites, how young is the company, how many games have they created before etc..

This is our first real product, of course there will be mistakes, boring things and disaster but the great thing with software is that you can change it after it has been released.

Those people that buy this game as it is today, consider yourself "baby-adopters". This game will not be the same one you bought in a few months. 

Squadleader32 out,

notes.title: Why and why not
notes.notes:
I realize that some people are a bit concerned regarding the fact that I didn't set this game as a "early-access" version.

I however, want to point out a few things that might clearify this.

I love critisism and I support everyone who wants to make their voice heard here.

The game was ticked as an "early-access" just yesterday, before the release. However, I changed that to a full-version release. 

Maybe that was a stupid mistake, maybe not. But this version that is out now is a fully playable game, and I don't have any intentions of making changes according to suggestions since I already have a lot of ideas that I want to implement to this game. 

*However, I am not saying that I don't want suggestions, I am just saying that this release was not intended for the community to follow the game as it progresses.*

We have a finalized version, and I thought it was a better way to show you what is coming and to make you exited - and to play the game and enjoy it as it is right now.

I'll be honest with you, I am not a developer in my "base-knowledge". I am a 20 year old guy who has created 2 companies in order to change the world. HJO Creations is working towards sustainability and creativity in these sort of areas. 

My goal is to create 3 high quality games.

1. Hands on Deck
2. RoboDome
3. Planetize

I am going to do everything I can in order to make these games as unique as possible, this is my first time I am launching a game such as this on Steam, I am learning and I will now know how to proceed with my future games thanks to you guys!

I appreciate every word and every opinion you have on this game and I will make sure to deliver what you ask for.

Squadleader32 out,

notes.title: We are planning to make this game *HUGE*
notes.notes:
The first idea was to create a game with inspiration from Overboard, 

The old game did not have multiplayer - So we didn't have that in our planning at first.

But since I have been the main developer of this game, I just can't stop thinking on all the things I want to add to this.

I really can't sleep on the nights because I come up with 20+ ideas that I can implement into this game.

So, this is a finished version of what we wanted the game to be from the beginning. But since I want a lot more. I figured I would tell you that and make this game into a original idea.

What you can expect in the very near future is:

*Car racing
*Motorboats gameplay in a pirate city
*Pirate gameplay (be a pirate)
*Airplane chase
*Submarine undercover

It's just I really want this to be an amazing game with as much creativity as possible + features that has never been seen in such a game as this before.

Squadleader32 out,

notes.title: Why not early access?
notes.notes:
Well, believe or not. The game was actually set to be in the early access page. 

But we talked with Steam and decided that this game is a finished game, as of how it looks right now.

It's a fully playable game with 400 mb of content (rougly). The multiplayer-functionalities and the other content are things we will add this week.

It's like saying that "this product will be updated A LOT" - there will be new stuff coming almost everyday. Becuase we really want to make this amazing.

In the "Early access" FAQ it says:

"Don't launch in Early Access if you are done with development.
If you have all your gameplay defined already and are just looking for final bug testing, then Early Access isn’t the right place for that. You’ll probably just want to send out some keys to fans or do more internal playtesting. Early Access is intended as a place where customers can have impact on the game."

We have the gameplay defined already and the multiplayer is just a + that will be a future functionality.
